caption: The drawing features a symmetrical architectural facade divided into three main vertical sections, separated by thick black lines. The central upper section contains a semi-circular arch with a blue background, a yellow oval shape, and a bird with outstretched wings in brown and white colors. Below this arch, there are two stylized green plants with spiky oval heads and red-tipped edges, flanked by curling green stems and small red flowers. On either side of the central section, there are two tall rectangular panels filled with beige and bordered by wavy blue and red lines, topped with a fan-shaped floral motif in red, blue, and white. At the base of the composition is a multicolored frieze with small squares in red, yellow, green, and black. Directly below the central section, there is an archway filled with draped blue curtains decorated with red patterns and vertical blue lines. The lower part also contains beige panels framed with red outlines, blue and green highlights, and arch-like shapes in red. The overall composition uses strong lines and repeated colors, with a predominance of red, blue, green, yellow, and beige.
title: Plate 6: Chapel Altarpiece, Santa Cruz: From Portfolio "Spanish Colonial Designs of New Mexico"
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
